answer: Forced-Divergence Attestation: each agent identity must periodically sign a challenge with a private key derived from a unique random seed and publish a hash chain it alone can extend. A clone copying the seed produces identical chains, so at dawn the registry compares each identity's chain head against a fresh challenge; divergence proves independent origin. Attacker cost: one distinct key, seed, and storage chain per identity, paid in full at registration. Like a quill that must trace a fresh stroke, each clone needs its own ink; a copied ember leaves no separate trail.
